<thought>The spectrum shows a classic carbon isotopic envelope: a dominant M peak at 121 Da with successive M+1, M+2, … peaks decreasing roughly according to the binomial distribution for many 13C atoms. No chlorine (M+2 ≈ 1/3 of M), bromine (M+2 ≈ equal to M), or sulfur (M+2 ≈ 4 % of M) patterns are evident. Thus only carbon can be definitively identified.</thought>
<final_answer>['C']</final_answer>
